'''''Phoenix sylvestris'''''  (''sylvestris'' - Latin, of the forest) also known as '''silver date palm''', '''Indian date''', '''sugar date palm''' or '''wild date palm''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate = 10 January 2017 }}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Arecaceae|palm]] family native to southern Pakistan, most of India, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and Bangladesh. It has been introduced to southeastern China, Sri Lanka, [[Mauritius]], [[Puerto Rico]] and the [[Leeward Islands]].<ref name=POWO/> Growing in plains and scrubland up to 1300 m above sea level, the [[fruit]] from this palm species is used to make wine and jelly. The [[sap]] is tapped and drunk fresh or fermented into toddy. The fresh sap is boiled to make palm [[jaggery]] in [[West Bengal]] state of India and Bangladesh.
[[File:COLLECTING DATE SAP.JPG|thumb|right|Preparing to collect sap at [[Jessore]], Bangladesh]]

==Description==
''Phoenix sylvestris'' ranges from {{Convert abbreviated|4 to 15|m}} in height and {{Convert abbreviated|40|cm}} in diameter; not as large as the [[Phoenix canariensis|Canary Island date palm]], but nearly so, and resembling it. The [[leaf|leaves]] are {{Convert abbreviated|3|m}} long, gently recurved, on {{Convert abbreviated|1|m|ft}} [[petiole (botany)|petioles]] with acanthophylls near the base.  The leaf crown grows to {{Convert abbreviated|10|m}} wide and {{Convert abbreviated|7.5 to 10|m}} tall containing up to 100 leaves. The inflorescence grows to 1 metre with white, unisexual flowers forming to a large, pendent infructescence. The single-seeded fruit ripens to a purple-red colour.<ref name=riffle>Riffle, Robert L. and Craft, Paul (2003) ''An Encyclopedia of Cultivated Palms''. Portland: Timber Press. (Pages 405-406) {{ISBN|0-88192-558-6}} / {{ISBN|978-0-88192-558-6}}</ref>
